authorization: Hunter requested importing the ten selected illustrations and associating them with the corresponding enters-tapped, scry-1 temple lands. Preserve all 309 main slots; five allied-pair temples remain separate candidates.

selections.title: The Parthenon
selections.credit: Art: Frederic Edwin Church · The Met
selections.cropNotes: Retain the colonnade and open sky; reduce foreground rubble before cutting the building. Actual Athena sanctuary depicted as a later ruin, not a reconstruction of the heroic age.

selections.title: Temple of Mercury
selections.credit: Art: Miner Kilbourne Kellogg · Smithsonian American Art Museum
selections.cropNotes: Preserve the temple and water setting. Mercury is the name in the museum title; precise archaeological site and original dedication remain unconfirmed. Do not present this as an archaeologically verified sanctuary of Hermes.

selections.title: The Sanctuary of Hercules
selections.credit: Art: Arnold Böcklin · National Gallery of Art
selections.cropNotes: The original is explicitly a sanctuary of Hercules, NOT Ares. The Ares association is a creative reassignment. Preserve the soldiers, enclosing wall and storm-dark grove.

selections.title: The Colossus of Rhodes / Colossus Solis
selections.artist: Philips Galle, after Maarten van Heemskerck
selections.credit: Art: Philips Galle, after Maarten van Heemskerck · Rijksmuseum
selections.cropNotes: A Renaissance imagining of Helios's monument, not a secure archaeological reconstruction. Retain the standing colossus and harbour; reduce the fallen-head episode and printed caption where possible.

selections.title: The Temple of Segesta with the Artist Sketching
selections.credit: Art: Thomas Cole · Museum of Fine Arts, Boston
selections.cropNotes: This is Segesta, NOT a documented temple of Demeter. Preserve the temple's relationship with vegetation and countryside. Demeter is our thematic reassignment; seek a larger reproduction before print lock.

selections.title: Island of the Dead
selections.cropNotes: Use the 1880 Met version, not the Berlin third version already catalogued as ART-292. Symbolic funerary landscape, not a literal Greek cult site. Keep the arriving boat, cypresses and tomb entrances; check dark-image legibility at card size.

selections.title: Temple of Poseidon at Cape Sounion
selections.institution: Holding collection unconfirmed; Wikimedia Commons reproduction
selections.cropNotes: A literal Poseidon temple. Preserve both the temple and coastal setting. Holding collection unconfirmed; the surviving Classical temple is later than the heroic setting.

selections.title: The Sacred Grove / Der heilige Hain
selections.cropNotes: The original does not explicitly depict Persephone. Preserve the ritual grouping and tree canopy; use the grove itself as sanctuary. Reproduction credit: Kunstmuseum Basel, Martin P. Bühler.

selections.title: The Statue of Zeus at Olympia
selections.artist: Philips Galle, after Maarten van Heemskerck
selections.credit: Art: Philips Galle, after Maarten van Heemskerck · Rijksmuseum
selections.matchType: Imagined reconstruction of a real sanctuary
selections.cropNotes: Use the separate Rijksmuseum Zeus record RP-P-2005-214-26-1 for the subject and attribution; the Commons crop filename inherits its parent album leaf's -26-2 metadata. Renaissance imagining, not an archaeological reconstruction. Emphasise the throne and temple; reduce foreground athletics.

selections.title: Ulysses at the Palace of Circe
selections.artist: Wilhelm Schubert van Ehrenberg; animals by Carl Borromäus Andreas Ruthart
selections.rights: Public-domain artwork / Getty Open Content reproduction
selections.credit: Art: W. S. van Ehrenberg & C. B. A. Ruthart · Getty Museum
selections.cropNotes: Direct Book X subject: Circe's palace and transformed animals. The palace functions as the sanctuary, not an attested temple; architecture is a seventeenth-century interpretation. Preserve palace, gardens and animals; keep narrative figures secondary.
